assumptions: Field labels (holder range, element stride, control counts) describe observed pointer arithmetic only, not confirmed source-level types.
Sized-delete sizes are the second argument observed at each PLT call site.

The sentinel-path virtual slots (+0x10 dispose, +0x18 destroy) are recorded as call-shape only: their targets depend on the control block's table, which this routine never reads except through those slots.
behavior: shared-release array teardown: per 0x40-byte element, release the shared control block at element+0x38 with full _Sp_counted_base release semantics, then dispose the string at element+0x08; finally free the holder buffer or return plainly when it is null. Never reads a holder table slot, never frees the holder itself, performs no canary check.

consumers.note: Reached only by code, never by data. See callers.tsv for the site list.

control_layout.count_field: +0x08 combined 64-bit value: low 32 bits use count, high 32 bits weak count
control_layout.table_field: +0x00 table pointer, read only on the sentinel path

flag_slot.rule: byte nonzero: plain decrement; byte zero: LOCK XADD decrement; observable results identical in both modes

observations: No direct or PLT call other than helper 0x5d35070 and the sized-delete PLT 0x63f0d80.
The sentinel arm (combined count 0x100000001) zeroes the whole count and calls the dispose table slot (+0x10) then the destroy table slot (+0x18) directly, without the helper.

Helper 0x5d35070 (76 bytes, verified separately) calls the dispose table slot (+0x10), decrements the weak count with the same single-threaded rule, and tail-dispatches the destroy table slot (+0x18) only when the old weak count was 1.
When reached from this routine, the helper's destroy arm cannot fire: (use, weak) == (1, 1) is intercepted by the sentinel path first, so any old weak count seen by the helper differs from 1.
A zero use count wraps to 2**32 - 1 with no dispose call.

The plain and locked decrement shapes are the same release used by the shared-copy increment routine 0x5d50400 (covered by #2712), which reads the same flag slot: increment on one side, decrement on this side.

Distinct from the neighbouring record-loop teardown 0x5d591d0: that routine walks 0x218-byte records with a +0x210 pointer and string vectors; this routine walks a flat 0x40-byte element array with a control-block release plus one string per element and no record fields.

phases.action: loop head: while cursor != end, stride 0x40; an empty range skips straight to the buffer exit
when the +0x38 pointer is null, skip the release and go to the string step

combined count == 0x100000001: zero the count, call dispose table slot +0x10, then destroy table slot +0x18; else decrement the use count (plain or LOCK XADD per the flag slot) and, when the old use count was 1, call helper 0x5d35070
short form (pointer == element+0x18) frees nothing; else sized delete (pointer, capacity + 1) with capacity at element+0x18
free (begin, +0x10 - begin) via tail jump to the sized-delete PLT when begin is non-null; plain return when begin is null; the +0x08 end is not reset

string_rule.heap_form: sized delete (pointer, capacity + 1), capacity at string + 0x10
string_rule.short_form: data pointer equals string address + 0x10; frees nothing

unknowns: The semantic roles of the dispose/destroy table slots beyond their positions are not pinned; they are recorded as call-shape only on the sentinel path.
What the six caller functions do with the holder before or after this call is not claimed; only the call sites and their FDEs are recorded.
